methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series F → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.3x) to $5.4B last post money.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Climate & Energy (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 2 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 8 same-sector peers exist in Climate & Energy, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Helion, a Series F frontier-energy company founded by David Kirtley and Chris Pihl, is evaluated against a broader Climate & Energy peer set of nine companies—one public (LNZA) and eight private firms including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix. A narrow same-stage or adjacent-stage peer universe proved insufficient to support median-based valuation, as no cohort of three or more identically-positioned comparables exists.

The Stage-Progression method was the applicable triangulation approach. Using Helion's last post-money valuation of $5.4B as the base, a typical Series F step-up multiplier of 1.3x yields an implied valuation of $7.0B. This method assumes conventional venture capital progression dynamics hold for frontier-technology financing. No other quantitative methods produced reliable signals given data constraints.

Analysis supports a valuation range of $6.0B to $8.1B, with a median point estimate of $7.0B. The current stated valuation of $15.5B sits substantially above this triangulated range, reflecting either material undisclosed progress, non-standard financing terms, or valuation methodology divergence. Primary uncertainties include the reliability of stage-progression multipliers in capital-intensive deep tech, the absence of narrow-peer comparables to stress-test assumptions, and the potential for sector-specific risk factors not captured in traditional venture metrics.
